column1: # Book 3 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). 3.1084 rejected: hiantis is accusative with the understood nos (Bailey, 'holds us ever gaping').

column2: a weight lies in the mind, wearing them out with its heaviness,
they would not live their lives as now we mostly see them,
who is weary to death of home, and suddenly comes back,
So each man flees himself, yet that self, as happens, of course,
he cannot escape; it clings against his will, and he hates it, {{NOTE: "ingratius" as printed; rendered as Bailey's "ingratis", "against his will"}}
because, sick as he is, he does not grasp the cause of his disease;
the rest; then, when that has come, we long for something else,
Therefore you may live out as many generations as you like;
